evidence.text_snippet: To fill the LUTs several CIT (measurements have been performed in an ARC  (ES-ARC, Thermal Hazard Technology) combined with a battery cycler (GSM, BaSyTec GmbH) at different environmental temperatures under isoperibolic conditions.

During the CIT measurement , a cell is first charged to 100% SOC and then discharged by rectangular current pulses of specified amplitude and length (as shown in Fig.4a)), which correspond to a decrease of the SOC  of the cell by a well -defined amount .
These measurements were carried out on the cell and the pack in a temperature chamber (Voetsch VT3 4018) with a battery cycler (BaSyTec HPS).
The cell under consideration was a commercial 18650 cell with LiMn2O4 cathode, a nominal cell capacity  1600 mAh and a nominal cell voltage of 3.7 V.

qualitative_findings: Under isoperibolic conditions, the temperature of the calorimeter chamber is kept constant, whereas the cell temperature can vary.
The deviation in temperature curves for the single cell under NEDC driving cycle was only 0.5 K.
The battery pack consists of six cells in series (6s1p).
The model and parameters are the same for all cells in the pack, differing slightly in nominal capacity and initial SOC.
Good quantitative agreement was found between measurements and simulation for NEDC.

extraction_notes: Cells used are commercial 18650 cells. Consequently, synthesis, electrode fabrication, and cell assembly parameters are not available in the text.
Current Interruption Technique (CIT) was used in place of traditional Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) to determine ECM parameters.
